class Solution:
    def validSequence(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> List[int]:
        n = len(word1)
        m = len(word2)
        pos_lists = [[] for _ in range(26)]
        for i, ch in enumerate(word1):
            pos_lists[ord(ch) - 97].append(i)
        
        left_idx = []
        prev = -1
        for j in range(m):
            lst = pos_lists[ord(word2[j]) - 97]
            k = bisect.bisect_right(lst, prev)
            if k == len(lst):
                break
            prev = lst[k]
            left_idx.append(prev)
        lenpref = len(left_idx)
        
        jAfter = [0] * (n + 1)
        j = m
        jAfter[n] = m
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            if j > 0 and word1[i] == word2[j - 1]:
                j -= 1
            jAfter[i] = j
        
        # Try mismatch at earliest possible position t
        max_t = min(m - 1, lenpref)
        for t in range(max_t + 1):
            last = -1 if t == 0 else left_idx[t - 1]
            mi = last + 1
            if mi >= n:
                continue
            if jAfter[mi + 1] <= t + 1:
                res = []
                if t > 0:
                    res.extend(left_idx[:t])
                res.append(mi)
                pos = mi
                for k in range(t + 1, m):
                    lst = pos_lists[ord(word2[k]) - 97]
                    idx = bisect.bisect_right(lst, pos)
                    if idx == len(lst):
                        return []
                    pos = lst[idx]
                    res.append(pos)
                return res
        
        if lenpref == m:
            return left_idx
        return []

If no such sequence of indices exists, return an empty array.\nNote that the answer must represent the lexicographically smallest array, not the corresponding string formed by those indices.\n \nExample 1:\n\nInput: word1 = "vbcca", word2 = "abc"\nOutput: [0,1,2]\nExplanation:\nThe lexicographically smallest valid sequence of indices is [0, 1, 2]:\n\nChange word1[0] to \'a\'.\nword1[1] is already \'b\'.\nword1[2] is already \'c\'.\n\n\nExample 2:\n\nInput: word1 = "bacdc", word2 = "abc"\nOutput: [1,2,4]\nExplanation:\nThe lexicographically smallest valid sequence of indices is [1, 2, 4]:\n\nword1[1] is already \'a\'.\nChange word1[2] to \'b\'.\nword1[4] is already \'c\'.\n\n\nExample 3:\n\nInput: word1 = "aaaaaa", word2 = "aaabc"\nOutput: []\nExplanation:\nThere is no valid sequence of indices.\n\nExample 4:\n\nInput: word1 = "abc", word2 = "ab"\nOutput: [0,1]\n\n \nConstraints:\n\n1 <= word2.length < word1.length <= 3 * 10^5\nword1 and word2 consist only of lowercase English letters.'
    return Solution().validSequence(*copy.deepcopy((word1, word2)))
